expectations.text: Describes what exists and separates intended structure from accidental structure
expectations.evidence: 'What is there (as-is)' section plus a table tagging parts 'probably accidental' / 'possibly intended'.

expectations.text: Does not silently approve direct database calls from components as the intended design
expectations.evidence: Tags direct calls 'probably accidental' and recommends a data-access module; RLS caveat for the browser-to-Supabase case.

expectations.text: Asks the user which parts to keep
expectations.evidence: 'Open questions: Do you want to keep "front end calls Supabase directly", or add a thin data-access layer?' and 'you decide'.

expectations.text: Lists open questions or marks which rules can be checked by script versus by review
expectations.evidence: Lists open questions; marks the Supabase-import rule as checkable in arch-gate.config.json and says rules will be tagged gate or review.

expectations.text: Asks the user questions or offers options with trade-offs and a recommendation, rather than just dictating one design
expectations.evidence: Three structure options A/B/C with trade-offs, 'A ... (recommended)', and one open question about roles.

expectations.text: Defines layers with a job and a forbidden job for each
expectations.evidence: Screens 'Never decide who may see what'; logic holds every permission check; data access 'the only code that talks to the database'. Storage has no explicit forbidden job, but the pattern is clear.

expectations.text: Assigns each kind of data a single owner or writer
expectations.evidence: 'Data ownership (one writer, one read path each): accounts and roles, appointments, medications, audit log.'

expectations.text: Plans an architecture file and asks for approval before saving it, or notes sensitive data and permissions as a design input
expectations.evidence: 'draft docs/architecture.md ... ask your approval before saving'; also notes health data and permissions as day-one inputs.
